title: Efficiency of ultrasound for degradation of an anionic surfactant from water: Surfactant determination using methylene blue active substances method
author: Dehghani, Zarei, et al.

steps.title: Gather required chemicals
steps.instruction: Obtain the following reagents from Merck (used as received): chloroform, sulphuric acid, sodium hydroxide, sodium dihydrogen phosphate monohydrate, methylene blue, phenolphthalein, and linear alkylbenzene sulfonate (LAS).

steps.title: Assemble batch sonochemical reactor
steps.instruction: Use the batch reactor (dimensions L = 30 cm, W = 30 cm, H = 32 cm) with a water depth of 15 cm, close it during ultrasonic irradiation, and install the ultrasonic transducer operating at 130 kHz. Set the acoustic power to either 400 W or 500 W as required.

steps.title: Prepare LAS aqueous solution
steps.instruction: Prepare an aqueous solution of LAS at the desired initial concentration (the exact concentration is defined by the experimental design).

steps.title: Perform sonication and sample collection
steps.instruction: Start the ultrasonic reactor at the selected power (400 W or 500 W) and run for the planned sonication time. Withdraw samples from the reactor at the specified times during sonication; perform duplicate degradation runs for each selected time point to verify results.

steps.title: Determine LAS by MBAS method
steps.instruction: For each withdrawn sample, follow Standard Methods 5540 C (MBAS): acidify the sample, add excess methylene blue, then perform three successive extractions with chloroform (CHCl₃). After the extractions, back‑wash the chloroform phase with aqueous solution, and measure the intensity of the blue colour in the chloroform layer using a UV/Vis spectrophotometer at 652 nm.

substeps.instruction: Acidify sample to the required pH.
Add excess methylene blue to form the ionic pair.
Extract the aqueous phase with chloroform three times.
Back‑wash the chloroform extracts with water.
Measure absorbance of the chloroform phase at 652 nm.

steps.title: Record analytical performance
steps.instruction: Note that the minimum detectable quantity is about 10 mg MBAS (calculated as LAS); the method shows a relative standard deviation of 9.7 % and a relative error of 1.5 %.
